A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CLIPFUSION. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original CLIPFUSION benchmark results, ablations, inference timings and qualitative examples, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: PatchCLIP, VV-attention, MapDiff's empty-mask feature extraction, memory-bank comparisons and anomaly-score fusion remain unchanged. Revised explanations do not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate anomaly segmentation and classification on the same MVTec-AD and VisA categories, retaining zero-shot, few-shot and one-for-all scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same task-specific participation of CLIP-AC, Trans-MM, MaskCLIP, PaDiM, PatchCore, WinCLIP and PromptAD. IIPAD remains the one-for-all comparator; the newly cited VCP-CLIP is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The benchmark splits, preprocessing, metrics, backbones, shot counts, selected fusion weights and latency-testing conditions are retained. Appendix A.2 adds documentation of weight selection without reporting a revision to the existing benchmark settings.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a brief sensitivity discussion covering five fusion-weight pairs and their task-dependent suitability, without a new numerical sweep table. Existing model, modality, extraction, prompt and training-sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both report means and standard deviations over five runs with different seeds. The Seed10/Seed20 training curves are unchanged; their consolidation into one figure does not change uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–21, including the exchanged numbering of Tables 7–8, and all plotted and qualitative results are unchanged. Appendix A.2 newly reports a qualitative finding from the five-pair weight comparison, favoring diffusion-heavy weighting for segmentation and CLIP-heavy weighting for classification.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions and equations are retained. V1 Appendix A's diffusion equations move into v2 Section 3 as Equations 2–3; this relocation introduces no new derivation or theoretical result.

C1.justification: V2 removes the explicit claim that this is the first approach to construct anomaly maps directly from diffusion cross-attention and feature maps. The central claims of complementary fusion, training-free operation and broad anomaly-detection performance remain.

C2.justification: V1 Appendix E's limitation concerning reduced adaptability to domain-specific anomalies, and its proposed fine-tuning direction, are absent in v2. The introduction also qualifies fusion as potentially beneficial where v1 called it essential.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies five candidate fusion-weight pairs, the A100 GPU's 40 GB memory and the decoder's four blocks numbered 0–3. Existing preprocessing, prompts, software and access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Qu et al.'s VCP-CLIP to the discussion of methods using auxiliary data and removes the explicit priority claim. The remaining related-work coverage is retained; citation-style changes do not add research coverage.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites the abstract, contributions and method explanations, moves diffusion preliminaries into Section 3, exchanges the inference-speed and one-for-all subsections, and reorganizes the appendices. It also corrects Section 5.2's Table 13 reference to Table 2.

P2.justification: The document adopts substantially different typography, margins, author formatting and float placement. Figures 1 and 3 become larger standalone displays, and v1 Figures 4–5 become the two panels of v2 Figure 4. The underlying visual evidence is preserved.

improvement.justification: V2 improves navigation, moderates the priority claim and adds limited tuning and hardware documentation. However, deleting v1 Appendix E removes an explicit qualification about domain-specific adaptability. These modest benefits and the loss of applicability discussion do not establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
